items.excerpt: A new report says OpenAI and Jony Ive's io first hardware device will be a portable, screenless smart speaker with a camera and sensors that read the user's surroundings — pitched as an AI-first 'home computer' rather than a phone-style gadget.

Bloomberg reporting recasts the much-hyped OpenAI x Jony Ive gadget as 'a smart speaker that moves' — portable, screenless, with mechanical parts meant to make it feel 'alive,' priced around $200-$300 and not shipping before 2027.

Ahead of the July 22 Galaxy Unpacked, Samsung teased the Galaxy Watch 9 and Watch Ultra 2 as an 'AI-powered health companion' promising real-time AI health insights, better tracking accuracy and new internal hardware.

Samsung's teaser frames the next Galaxy Watch as a 'health-first, always-on gateway for advanced, personalized AI,' continuously tracking wellness metrics — a push to make on-wrist AI health the headline of Unpacked.

Samsung's health notice signals One UI 9 Watch arriving this month, adding an AI-driven Blood Pressure Trend feature to Galaxy Watches while retiring Vascular Load in the US — a shift in the watch's on-device health-sensing stack.

HMD launched four Nokia-badged 4G feature phones with a dedicated AI button that triggers an on-device Sikey AI voice assistant for torch, alarms, reminders and calls — a curious low-end take on putting AI in your hand (with a subscription after 180 days).

Meta is adding rate limits to AI features on its Ray-Ban smart glasses, capping Conversation Focus at three hours a month free and gating 15 hours behind a $20/month Meta One Premium plan — an early sign of AI-glasses features moving to subscriptions.
